title: Bounded register subtraction run
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let $B$ be a natural number, let $b$ be a Boolean value, and let $st$ be a seven-register state whose registers $K,S,P,T,Z,C,V$ are all at most $B$. The program has a finite run from label $	ext{sb}(b,0)$ with registers initialized from $st$ to label $	ext{jzC}(b)$, with the same registers as $st$ except that $V$ is set to $0$ and $C$ is set to the truncated difference $	ext{max}(C-V,0)$; every configuration before the endpoint satisfies the program guard and has all registers at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: All seven registers of $st$ are at most $B$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, let $B$ be a natural number, let $b$ be a Boolean value, and
let $st$ be a state whose seven register values $K,S,P,T,Z,C,V$ are each at most $B$.
Starting from the configuration with control label $\mathrm{sb}(b,0)$ and register
values given by $st$, the program reaches the label that tests whether $C=K-V$ with
register values given by $st$, except that $V$ is set to $0$ and $C$ to the truncated
difference of its original value and the original value of $V$; every configuration
before the endpoint satisfies the program precondition and has all register values at
most $B$.
